name: Western Schism begins
summary: On the death of Pope Gregory XI (1378), the first pope to return to Rome after the Avignon period, a disputed election produces two popes: Urban VI in Rome and Clement VII in Avignon. For 39 years, the Latin Church has two (and eventually three) simultaneous claimants to the papacy. National loyalties determine allegiance: France, Castile, Scotland, and Naples support the Avignon papacy; England, Germany, Hungary, and Italy support Rome. The Council of Constance (1414–1418) resolves the schism but permanently damages papal moral authority.

_quarry.structural_significance: Destroys the papacy's moral authority at a critical moment; demonstrates the limitation of papal power when national interests override religious unity; contributes to the conditions that make the Protestant Reformation possible
